key_insight: Robot task success rates alone cannot explain how AI agents succeed or where they fail. AgentRoboCritic introduces action-level analysis to examine frontier agents’ direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks summarize performance at the episode level, hiding the individual low-level actions behind successful and failed robot behaviors.
method: Study frontier multimodal agents that control robots through low-level numerical actions rather than high-level primitives.
Analyze behavior at the action level across 12 manipulation benchmarks.
Introduce AgentRoboCritic for this analysis; the provided abstract is truncated, so its implementation and detailed results are unavailable.
impact: Action-level evaluation can help practitioners diagnose robot-control failures that aggregate success rates miss. It offers a more informative basis for comparing and improving embodied AI agents.
visual_elements: Control-loop diagram: visual observation → multimodal agent → numerical action → robot.
Side-by-side comparison of episode-level success scoring and action-level analysis.
Illustrative action timeline highlighting steps that could contribute to success or failure.
Grid representing the 12 manipulation benchmarks, without inventing task names or results.
paper_title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
paper_authors: Yiyang Du, Yuxuan Kuang, Qitao Zhao, Yixuan Wang, Zhanqiu Guo
